chapter_name: Chapter 03: Order of Words and Phrases
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn the standard syntactical order of English sentences, including the SVO rule, adverb placement, and the Royal Order of Adjectives.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Imagine putting on your shoes before your socks! In English, the order of words matters just as much. Change the order, and you change the entire meaning. Let's learn the secret formulas for perfect sentence structures! 🧪

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The standard English sentence follows a strict order: Subject (Who/What) ➡️ Verb (Action) ➡️ Object (Receives action). After the core, we place Adverbial Phrases in the order of M-P-T: Manner (How), Place (Where), and Time (When).
examples_or_templates: Subject + Verb + Object + Manner + Place + Time

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When using multiple adjectives before a noun, they must follow a specific sequence: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose (OSASCOMP). We rarely use more than three at once!
examples_or_templates: A beautiful (opinion), small (size), old (age), brown (color), wooden (material) box.
(Not: A wooden brown old beautiful small box!)

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Adverbs of Frequency (always, never, often) usually go BEFORE the main verb, but AFTER the 'to be' verb (is, am, are). Adverbs of degree (very, almost) go right before the adjective or adverb they modify.
examples_or_templates: Main verb: He ALWAYS arrives late.
'To be' verb: He is ALWAYS late.
Degree: The water is VERY cold.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which sequence of adjectives is in the correct order?
❓ What is the correct S-V-O-M-P-T order for these phrases: (1) quickly (2) the tiger (3) yesterday (4) chased (5) in the jungle (6) the deer

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rearrange the adjectives into the correct 'Royal Order': 'She bought a (leather / stylish / black / Italian) jacket.'
subjective_practice.hint: Opinion first, then Color, Origin, and Material last.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Place the adverb 'never' in the correct position in this sentence: 'I have seen such a massive storm.'
subjective_practice.hint: It should go between the helping verb 'have' and the main verb 'seen'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Unjumble the sentence using S-V-O-M-P-T: 'at the stadium / beautifully / played / the team / last night / football.'
subjective_practice.hint: Find the Subject and Verb first. Then ask: What? How? Where? When?

activity_or_assignment.title: 🛍️ The Adjective Auction
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Pick an object in your room (like a lamp or a shoe). Try to write a phrase describing it using 4 adjectives in the correct OSASCOMP order. Challenge a friend to read it aloud—if they stumble, your order might be wrong!

chapter_summary: ⭐ The standard sentence order is Subject + Verb + Object + Manner + Place + Time.
⭐ Multiple adjectives follow the OSASCOMP rule (Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose).
⭐ Adverbs of frequency generally go before the main verb, but after 'to be' verbs.
